answer.policy_title: Surgery of the Knee — UnitedHealthcare Commercial and Individual Exchange Medical Policy
answer.effective_date: September 10, 2026 (per the currently posted PDF). IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the denial notice is dated 2026-08-02, which is BEFORE this posted version's effective date. UHC revises this policy periodically (it has a 'Policy History/Revision Information' section), so the version actually applied to Quinn's 2026-08-02 determination was likely an earlier-numbered version of this same policy (e.g., a 2026 mid-year or 2025 version), not necessarily the 09/10/2026 version now online.
criteria_quotes: "Surgery of the knee is proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances. For medical necessity clinical coverage criteria, refer to the: InterQual® CP: Procedures: Arthroscopy or Arthroscopically Assisted Surgery, Knee..." (Coverage Rationale section)

CPT 29888 (Arthroscopically aided anterior cruciate ligament repair/augmentation or reconstruction) is listed in this policy's 'Applicable Codes' table, confirming it is the governing document for this procedure.

The policy's own text does NOT spell out the specific conservative-treatment trial requirements (e.g., duration of physical therapy, bracing, activity modification). Instead, it delegates the actual clinical decision criteria to InterQual® CP: Arthroscopy or Arthroscopically Assisted Surgery, Knee — a proprietary, licensed criteria set owned by a third-party vendor (Change Healthcare/InterQual), which is not published in full text in this PDF or otherwise publicly available online. The policy states only: 'Click here to view the InterQual® criteria,' which links to a login-gated provider tool, not public text.
answer.appeal_deadline: 2027-01-29 (180 days from the 2026-08-02 notice date), as stated in the denial letter. This matches UnitedHealthcare's standard commercial member appeal window of 180 days from receipt of the denial.
answer.submission_route: Internal appeal: In writing to the address/fax printed on the specific denial letter or member ID card (this is the authoritative source — addresses vary by plan/line of business). A general UHC commercial member appeals address published by UHC is: UnitedHealthCare Member Inquiry/Appeals, P.O. Box 740816, Atlanta, GA 30374-0816. Appeals can also often be filed online via the member portal (member.uhc.com) or by phone (member services number on the ID card) requesting a formal written appeal. After exhausting UHC's internal appeal (or upon reaching final adverse determination), Minnesota law gives the member the right to an external review: for insurance-company plans, filed with the Minnesota Department of Commerce (Attn: Consumer Protection & Education Division, 85 7th Place East, Suite 500, St. Paul, MN); for HMO-licensed plans, filed with the Minnesota Department of Health. External review generally must be requested within a set window (commonly ~6 months of the final internal denial) and may carry a modest filing fee (e.g., $25, per MN AG consumer guidance) that is waived for indigent enrollees.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: Because the specific medical-necessity criteria (the required conservative-treatment trial elements) are contained in the InterQual® CP 'Arthroscopy or Arthroscopically Assisted Surgery, Knee' guideline — a licensed, proprietary product — the patient/provider should: (1) call the number on the denial letter/ID card and explicitly request 'the full text of the InterQual criteria (or equivalent clinical review criteria) applied to this determination,' which ACA/ERISA and Minnesota law generally require the plan to provide free of charge upon request for an adverse benefit determination; (2) ask the treating orthopedic surgeon's office to request the same from UHC's provider portal (UHCprovider.com), since providers can access InterQual criteria directly if their organization has an InterQual/UHC provider login; (3) request the specific version/date of the 'Surgery of the Knee' medical policy that was in effect on 2026-08-02 (not just the current 09/10/2026 version), since UHC policies are dated and revised.
answer.notes: High confidence that 'Surgery of the Knee,' Policy Number 2026T0553JJ (or its immediately prior revision), is the correct governing UHC document for CPT 29888 in the Commercial/Individual Exchange line of business — it explicitly lists 29888 in its Applicable Codes table and is the only UHC medical policy addressing knee ligament/arthroscopic surgery medical necessity for commercial members. However, two limitations reduce full confidence: (1) the publicly posted PDF's effective date (09/10/2026) postdates the 2026-08-02 denial letter, so the exact policy number/version actually cited by the reviewer may differ slightly (this is a recurring, quarterly-revised UHC policy family, same title); (2) the actual line-item medical necessity criteria that the denial reason ('inadequate trial of conservative treatment') maps to live inside InterQual® proprietary criteria referenced by, but not reproduced in, the public policy — I could not retrieve that InterQual text because it sits behind a licensed/login-gated system, so I have not fabricated specific duration/PT-visit thresholds. The patient's appeal should demand the plan disclose the specific InterQual criteria and specific documentation gaps it says are missing, as they are entitled to under the adverse benefit determination notice requirements.

NOTICE OF ADVERSE BENEFIT DETERMINATION

Date of notice: 2026-08-02
Member: Quinn Grant
Member ID: W553544386
Plan: UnitedHealthcare (Commercial/ACA), state of Minnesota

Dear Quinn,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Requested service: ACL reconstruction
    Procedure code (CPT): 29888

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-01-29).

Reference number: POC-87E365CAED-66145

Note: UHC will accept three or more moderate to severe radiographic findings to be sufficient to support the diagnosis of severe osteoarthritis (American College of Radiology, 2025). Reduced Allograft Discs [e.g., Cartiform (Arthrex), ProChondrix CR (Allosource)]: Wafer-thin allografts in which the bony portion of the allograft is reduced. The discs contain hyaline cartilage with chondrocytes, growth factors, and extracellular matrix proteins. Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Arthritis Index: The WOMAC is a disease-specific, self-administered questionnaire developed to evaluate individuals with hip or knee osteoarthritis. It uses a multidimensional scale composed of 24 items that are grouped into three dimensions: pain, stiffness, and physical function (Quintana et al., 2009).
